overview.mechanism: Valproate acts through multiple neuronal mechanisms, including GABAergic signaling and modulation of ion-channel activity; no single mechanism explains all clinical effects.
uses: Treatment of seizure disorders according to the approved formulation-specific indication.

paragraphs.text: Sodium valproate, valproic acid and divalproex deliver valproate but are not identical product formulations. Oral immediate-, delayed- and extended-release preparations and intravenous injection must not be assigned a common administration schedule from the generic name alone.
Important clinical risks include hepatotoxicity, thrombocytopenia and teratogenicity. Mechanistic or experimental benefits in other diseases do not justify widening approved indications.

Nonlinear protein binding and drug interactions complicate interpretation of concentrations. In kidney disease, a total concentration cannot always be assumed to represent the same unbound exposure as in a patient with normal binding. No new renal dose schedule is inferred here.
